title: Why Some Volcanoes Explode and Others Flow
post_title: Why Some Volcanoes Explode and Others Flow | QuantaTale
post_description: How magma forms and why gas decides whether a volcano flows or explodes, from USGS and NASA. Sources: United States Geological Survey https://www.usgs.gov/faqs/how-do-volcanoes-erupt and National Aeronautics and Space Administration https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/volcanoes/en/ #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: Why does one volcano pour out lava while another blows itself apart? Deep underground, some rock melts into a thick liquid called magma. Magma is lighter than the surrounding rock, so it rises and collects in chambers. When it pushes out through a vent to the surface, it is called lava. How explosive an eruption is depends on the magma's composition. Thin, runny magma lets gas escape easily, so it flows out of the volcano. Thick, sticky magma traps gas until the pressure builds and the volcano explodes. Earth has both explosive volcanoes and ones with slow rivers of lava.
